result_summary: Produced and reopened a dependency-aware Alumnos local campaign candidate. The plan identifies the actual bottleneck as missing durable root binding/routing plus local integration, not missing page UI; preserves José Study, Student World and PageKit/Class Player as distinct child authorities; reuses the canonical ALL_DEPENDENCIES_HAVE_RETURN local-Steward gate; and defers child product campaigns until authority/routing convergence instead of making José the root by inference.
material_advances: Separated current durable state, candidate root binding, historical guardrails and unresolved source debt.
Used the existing nine-dependency local integration gate rather than inventing a second scheduler or duplicate integration path.
Defined a five-stage campaign: parallel evidence convergence, derived local integration, root-binding/routing candidate, parallel child-owner campaigns, and verify/replan.

Defined the one-message correction flow from Alumnos surface through Page Change Thread, owner resolution, local planning, atomic worker claim, local Steward disposition and same-surface visible candidate.
Rejected making José Study the Alumnos root, building a generic teacher dashboard before root semantics, and serially waiting for peer workers.
Preserved shared/study/current.json as the reusable Study UI owner and prohibited implicit Current/Human Accepted/Served promotion.
Deduplicated against sibling Alumnos lenses, local Steward, Page Thread bridge, local integration and prior root-discovery handoff; emitted zero premature global queue items.
non_obvious_finding: The safest high-leverage next sequence is not teacher-page redesign. Existing pages are already reopenable; the missing compounding capability is the coordination root/routing boundary. UI-first work would risk collapsing José into project authority and increase human routing cost rather than remove it.
